messages.subject: Multidimensional IRT: Negative slopes
parts:
Hi,
I am new with MIRT and I may have gaps in my foundational understanding. Nevertheless, allow me to ask my question and feel free to point me to documentation or other link as necessary.

I am trying to fit a multidimensional (2 dimension) IRT model. There are 71 items in the dataset and for most of the items, both slops (a1 and a2) are negative. There are NA in the dataset. My reading from the plot tells me that, as student's ability increases (theta_1 and theta_2 increases), probability of getting an answer correct decreases. This does not make a lot of sense to me. What am i doing wrong?

Note that, when I fit those same data with a uni-dimensional IRT, slopes of item characteristic curve are positive (with the exception of 2 item). This makes perfect sense.

Can you kindly help me interpreting the negative slope of mirt model.

regards,
Azman Sami

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Multidimensional IRT: Negative slopes
parts:
Is the model you fit an exploratory or confirmatory factor analysis model? If the former this is quite common due to the rotational indeterminacy, and you could just multiply each axis by -1 to flip the signs for each dimension. If the latter, this would be more unusual given the starting values of mirt, but the same principle would apply. All latent variable models are effectively sign indeterminate if the identification isn't based on some anchoring item, and in IRT models we often use the default 0 mean 1 variance scaling, so this can crop up. HTH. 

Phil
